title: You thought the battle was equal.
paragraphs: You thought the battle was equal.
Like somehow you and the darkness were on the same level… trading blows, hoping you survive another day.
But that’s not what Scripture says.
Not even close.
There was a moment—quiet, almost easy to miss—when Jesus looked at ordinary, flawed men and said something that should have shattered every fear you’ve been carrying.
“I have given you authority… over all the power of the enemy, and nothing shall by any means hurt you.” (Luke 10:19)
Read that again.

Not some power.
Not most power.
All.
And yet you still feel bound.
You still feel attacked, overwhelmed, controlled by thoughts you didn’t ask for, habits you can’t seem to break, patterns that keep dragging you back into the same pit.

You pray, but there’s hesitation.
You resist, but there’s doubt.
Because deep down, you’re not sure if you actually have authority… or if that verse is just something nice to quote when things get hard.
But here’s what most people don’t realize…

Authority doesn’t come from your feelings.
It doesn’t come from your performance.
It doesn’t even come from how strong your faith feels in the moment.
It comes from a Person.
And if you are in Jesus Christ, then what He conquered… you stand in.
Originally written by Gospel Warrior.
The problem isn’t that the enemy is stronger than you.
The problem is you’ve been living like you’re still under him.

You let the accusation stay.
You let the temptation linger.
You entertain the lie just long enough for it to feel true.
And all the while, heaven is not confused about your position.

Colossians 2:15 says,
“He disarmed the rulers and authorities and put them to open shame, by triumphing over them in Him.”
Disarmed.
That means the enemy you’re terrified of has already been stripped.
So why does it still feel like he’s winning?
Because authority must be exercised.

Not in arrogance.
Not in noise.
But in truth.
Jesus didn’t say, “I will fight for you while you stay passive.”
He said, “I have given you authority.”
There’s a difference.
You remember that moment.

When you knew something was wrong.
When conviction hit you like a quiet warning.
But you ignored it.

God saw it.
You knew.
And instead of standing in what Christ gave you, you stepped back into what He already freed you from.
That’s where the tension lives.
Because on one side, there is the finished work of Jesus.
On the other… your daily surrender.
James 4:7 doesn’t say, “Ask the devil politely to leave.”

It says,
“Submit yourselves therefore to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.”

Submit.
Then resist.
Not the other way around.

Authority without surrender becomes pride.
Surrender without resistance becomes passivity.
And many people are stuck right there—praying for deliverance while refusing to confront what they’re entertaining.
But the Gospel doesn’t leave you in that cycle.
It confronts it.
You were not saved just to be forgiven.
You were saved to be transferred.
“Delivered from the domain of darkness and transferred to the kingdom of His beloved Son.” (Colossians 1:13)
That means your position changed.
Your identity changed.
Your authority changed.
But if your mind stays in the old place… your life will reflect it.
This is why the enemy fights your thoughts so aggressively.
Because if he can keep you believing you’re powerless, you will never use what Christ already gave you.
And then comes the breaking point.

The moment where you either keep agreeing with the lie…
or you finally stand in truth.
Not because you feel strong.
But because Jesus is.
You don’t rebuke darkness because you’re confident in yourself.
You do it because the One who lives in you has already overcome.
“Greater is He that is in you, than he that is in the world.” (1 John 4:4)
This is where everything shifts.

Because authority isn’t shouting louder.
It’s standing firmer.

It’s saying no when your flesh says yes.
It’s rejecting the thought before it builds a home.
It’s choosing obedience when compromise feels easier.
And yes… it costs something.
Because the version of you that keeps losing must die.

Jesus said,
“If anyone would come after Me, let him deny himself and take up his cross daily and follow Me.” (Luke 9:23)
Daily.
Not once.
Not when it’s convenient.
Daily.
That’s where authority becomes real.

Not in theory.
Not in posts.
But in the quiet decisions no one else sees.
And there are two futures sitting in front of you right now.
One where you keep living like a victim—saved, but stuck… forgiven, but powerless… constantly cycling through defeat.
And one where you begin to walk as what Scripture actually says you are—free, equipped, and unshaken… not because life is easy, but because your authority is rooted in Christ.
This isn’t about pretending the battle isn’t real.
It is.
But the outcome was already decided at the cross.
So the question is not whether Jesus has authority.
The question is whether you will actually live in it.
If something in you is stirring right now, don’t ignore it.
Say it plainly.
“I’ve been living below what Christ gave me.”
Own it.
And then turn.
That’s repentance—not just feeling bad, but changing direction.
Someone you know is silently losing battles they were never meant to fight alone.
And if you’re tired of shallow faith and surface-level truth, follow this path deeper.
Stay close. Stay submitted. Stay sharp.

Because this isn’t about inspiration.
It’s about transformation.
